pages.title: Agent Host & MessagePort RPC
pages.purpose: Document the Agent Host utilityProcess, its supervision/restart semantics, and the request/response + stream RPC protocol surface.
instructions: Describe HostManager: status lifecycle, ping/pong heartbeat, crash window, restart budget, and snapshot re-delivery on restart.
Explain the RPC wire protocol (request/response/subscribe/unsubscribe/event) and its timeout/error semantics.
Note the agent-host crash handling (uncaughtException exit, main supervision).
Summarize the Apis and Streams surfaces and typical flows (agent.new, agent.command, sessions.*, auth.*, skills/plugins).

pages.title: Built-in Browser Service
pages.purpose: Document the in-app Chromium browser: WebContentsView surface, profiles/tabs, agent authorization and confirmation flows, network policy, header rules, secret vault, downloads, and persistency.
instructions: Cover confirmation dialogs, header rules, network policy/interceptor, secret vault, redaction, and downloads.
Cover renderer controls exposed via piBridge.browser*. Describe capability snapshot sync to the Agent Host.
Describe the browser surface (WebContentsView) shared by user and agent, tabs, profiles, and tab restoration.
Explain the agent authorization model: Coding permissions do not imply browser rights; runtime session grants vs persistent session permissions.

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: Document supervised managed processes (posix and Windows-native), lifecycle, output buffering, loopback endpoints, and crash reaping.
instructions: Cover output buffering/log windows, loopback endpoints, readiness probing, and stop sources.
Describe shutdown cleanup and the reaper journal.
Describe the posix backend and the Windows native helper binary/contract, plus the reaper on main for crash recovery.
Explain the managed process lifecycle states and stop modes.

pages.title: Messaging Channels (Feishu / Telegram / WeChat)
pages.purpose: Document the external messaging channel adapters, account config, secret vault integration, lane scheduling, and the Pi session bridge.
instructions: Describe channel adapters for weixin, telegram, feishu/lark and the adapter registry.
Describe secret handling: secrets stored via OS credential vault through main, channel state/config stores.
Explain account configuration, DM/group policies, requireMention, slash commands, and inbound routing.
Explain the lane scheduler for outbound turns and the PiSessionBridge that drives agent runs.

pages.title: Architecture & Process Model
pages.purpose: Explain the overall desktop architecture: Electron main/renderer/preload, the supervised Agent Host utilityProcess, MessagePort RPC transport, and how the pieces connect.
instructions: Cover the renderer Reconnecting-to-Host recovery flow.
Describe main-process responsibilities (window, menus, tray, updates, Host supervision) and the Host's agent responsibilities.
Describe the process topology: Electron main process, sandboxed renderer with preload, and a utilityProcess Agent Host running pi-coding-agent.
Explain the no-internal-server MessagePort design and how ports are attached and transferred.

pages.title: Security & Trust Boundaries
pages.purpose: Document trust boundaries and security invariants: sandboxed renderer, IPC trust, credential vault, toolchain download integrity, browser isolation, and redaction.
instructions: Cover credential storage (safeStorage-backed vault), secret fingerprints, and redaction of secrets in logs.
Cover toolchain download integrity (sha256, signed catalog) and packaged toolchain verification.
Describe IPC sender trust validation and the renderer-to-Host vs app-owned-Host-to-toolchains distinction.
Explain the sandbox + contextIsolation renderer, preload location/message policies, and the compile-time security checks.

pages.title: Sessions, Files, Projects & Skills
pages.purpose: Document the agent session/file/project surface: session watching and indexing, file access policy, worktrees, git status, skills, and plugins.
instructions: Describe file access validation, allowed roots, file watching, and file suggestions.
Describe skills service (frontmatter/CLI) and plugins service (install/set via worker), plus the extension diagnostics.
Explain session storage watching under the pi agent directory and sessions.changed events.
Explain worktree and git-status APIs, project-tree discovery, and auto session titles.

pages.title: Toolchains & Developer Tools
pages.purpose: Document toolchain discovery, probing, managed component install/repair, profiles, cached execution snapshots, and how the Agent Host consumes them.
instructions: Describe discovery, candidate normalization/dedpe, probing, and default selection.
Describe how a ToolchainSnapshot is pushed to the Agent Host and resolved into command environments.
Explain the capability model (shell.bash, vcs.git, js.node, python.*, search.*, etc.), providers, preferences, and health states.
Explain the runtime catalog schema, managed component install/repair lifecycle, profiles, caches, and bundled core tools.

pages.title: Build, Test & Release Tooling
pages.purpose: Document packaging, verification gates, CI, and the supporting scripts and native Windows helper build.
instructions: Describe Windows native helper build and reproducibility checks, and the CI workflow.
Describe the verify.mjs quality gate ordering (format, lint, typecheck, tests, contract, security, build, smoke).
Explain packaging via electron-builder (asar, extraResources, toolchain catalogs), signing/notarization status, and the Verify scripts.
Explain the build pipeline (tsup main/preload/host, Vite renderer) and outputs.

pages.title: Desktop Window, Updates & App Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Document the desktop shell: window creation/state, menu/tray, deep links, single instance, app protocol, and the update manager.
instructions: Cover startup readiness gating and validation flags.
Describe the app menu, tray and badge, deep-link handling, single-instance lock, and custom app protocol.
Describe the update manager state machine, automatic checks, download watchdog, and install-on-quit gates (active sessions).
Explain main window creation, persisted window state/bounds, and renderer crash recovery.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical entry point: prerequisites, install, dev, build, test, package, and common workflows for engineers new to the repo.
instructions: Cover the engine/node version requirement (Node >=22.19.0 <23) and that it is a pure Electron app with no bundled Node server.
Explain how to install dependencies, run the dev loop (Vite + tsup watch + Electron), run lint/typecheck/tests, and produce packaged artifacts.
Point to the architecture and build/test pages for detail rather than duplicating them.
